該地區的癌症死亡人數已經增了一倍，這個事實說明官方對核電安全性所作的種種保證純屬一派胡言。

NONE: › to stop trying to guess
放棄猜測；認輸

example: You'll never guess the answer - do you give up?
你永遠也猜不到答案的——你認輸嗎？
I give up - how many were there?
我猜不出來了——到底有多少？

NONE: › to expect someone or something to fail
預期…將會失敗

example: Most people gave up on him when he dropped out, but he went back and earned his degree two years later.
當他退學時，大部分人都對他不再抱有期望，但是他後來回來了並在兩年後取得了學位。

NONE: › to stop owning and using something
放棄（某物的所有權或使用權）；交出；讓出
› to stop hoping that a particular thing will happen
不再抱有希望，放棄希望
B2 to stop doing something before you have finished it, usually because it is too difficult
（通常因為太難而）終止，放棄

example: They were forced to give up their home because they couldn't pay the mortgage.
他們因為還不起按揭貸款被迫交出房子。
We still haven't given up hope of finding her alive.
我們還沒有放棄她生還的希望。
[ + -ing verb ] I've given up trying to help her.
我已經放棄努力，不想再幫她了。

NONE: › to die
死，死去
› humorous If a machine gives up the ghost, it stops working.
（機器）壞了，不能運作，完蛋
› UK to stop trying to do something because you know that you will not succeed
放棄…；對…絕望

example: Our old TV had finally given up the ghost.
我們的老電視終於壞了。
All I'd cherished from early childhood had been denied me, so I simply gave up the ghost.
我自童年起所珍惜的一切都被奪走了，我只好放棄。

NONE: › to express your thoughts or feelings in words
表達（觀點或情感）

example: I always had doubts about the project but I never gave voice to them.
我一直對那個計劃存有疑慮，但我從來沒有說出來。

NONE: C1 UK US yield to allow other vehicles to go past before you move onto a road
讓（其他車輛）先行
C2 to break, especially when under pressure from strong forces
（尤指在很大的壓力下）坍塌，垮掉
› to stop arguing or fighting against someone or something
讓步，屈服

example: You have to give way to traffic coming from the right.
你要讓右邊駛來的車輛先行。
Because of an unusually strong current, the bridge's central support gave way, tipping a coach into the river.
因為遭遇罕見的湍急洪流的衝擊，橋中心的支座坍塌，一輛長途客車被掀進了河裡。
Neither of them will give way, so they could be arguing for a very long time.
他們兩個誰也不會讓步，所以他們會吵好長時間。
Don't give way to your fears.
不要怕。

NONE: C2 to be replaced by something, especially because it is better, cheaper, easier, etc.
被（更好的、更便宜的、更容易的等等）取代，淘汰

example: In some areas, modern intensive farming is giving way to the re-introduction of traditional methods.
在一些地區，現代集約式耕作正在被重新引進的傳統方法取代。

NONE: › If you would give your eyeteeth for something, you would like it very much.
非常喜歡…；非常想得到…

example: Most women would give their eyeteeth for hair like yours.
大部分女人都會非常渴望擁有你這樣的一頭秀髮。

NONE: › to continue to have a close involvement in a particular thing for the whole of your life
一心撲在…上，全身心投入到…中

example: She gave her life to cancer research.
她全身心地投入到癌症研究之中。

NONE: › If you say that you would give your right arm to do or have something, you mean you would like it very much.
不惜一切代價；（為了…）願捨棄很多

example: I would give my right arm to meet the president.
只要能見到總統，要甚麼我都給。

NONE: C1 to promise
承諾；保證

example: He gave his word that he would marry her and she had no cause to doubt him.
他保證會與她結婚，她沒有理由懷疑他。

NONE: › to spend all your time and energy doing or feeling something
致力於；沉溺於；放任自己（做某事）

example: After her death he gave himself over to grief.
她去世後，他沉溺在悲痛中不能自拔。

NONE: › to allow the police or an enemy to take you as a prisoner
投案，自首；投降

example: The gunman gave himself up to the police.
持槍歹徒向警察投降。
See also
give yourself over/up to sth

NONE: › in sports such as football and hockey, an occasion when a player passes the ball and then moves quickly into a position where they can receive the ball
（在足球和曲棍球等體育運動中）傳切配合

example: He played a perfect give-and-go with Alcacer before shooting from the edge of the box.
他和阿爾卡撒做了一個傳切配合然後在禁區角處射門。

NONE: › to develop and use emotions or ideas completely
充分發揮

example: The move from stage to movies allowed Gildit to give full play to his sense of the fantastic.
從舞臺轉到電影界，吉爾迪可以充分發揮他的幻想靈感。

NONE: › to allow someone to get something very easily, without having to work for it
輕易讓步；拱手相讓

example: If you sell your share in the company now, you're handing the ownership to him on a silver platter.
如果你現在出售你在公司的股權，就等於把所有權拱手讓給他。

NONE: › to allow someone to get or win something very easily
把…拱手讓給（某人）；讓（某人）輕鬆贏得

example: They were handed the contract on a plate.
他們很輕鬆地得到了合約。
The Canadian team handed the game to them on a plate.
加拿大隊讓他們輕易取勝。

NONE: › to help someone
助（某人）一臂之力，幫助（某人）

example: These tax cuts will give industry a helping hand.
這些減稅措施將會促進工業發展。

C: › something that is given free to a customer
› informal something that tells or shows something secret, often without intending to
顯露（某人）的感情；暴露（某人）的內心世界

NONE: › A giveaway price is very low.
（價格）低廉的

example: He said he'd given up smoking, but the empty packs in the bin were a dead giveaway (= clearly showed the secret truth).
他說他已經戒煙了，但是垃圾桶裡的空煙盒讓他徹底露了馬腳。
The furniture shop's offering three-piece suites at giveaway prices.
傢俱店正以極低的價格出售一組三件套裝傢俱。

NONE: › past participle of
give
› knowing about or considering a particular thing
考慮到，鑒於
› something that is certain to happen
（定當發生的）假設事實，假定事實
› already decided, arranged, or agreed
規定的；特定的；已經安排好的；已認可的
› to do something regularly or as a habit
經常做；習慣於

example: Given his age, he's a remarkably fast runner.
考慮到他的年齡，他可稱得上是個很出眾的賽跑運動員了。
Given (the fact) that he's had six months to do this, he hasn't made much progress.
鑒於他有六個月的時間完成這項工作，他並沒有取得太多進展。
At the given signal, the group rushed forward to the barrier.
預定信號一發出，人群便向關卡衝去。
The bomb could go off at any given (= any) time and in any given (= any) place.
炸彈隨時隨地都可能爆炸。
She was given to staying in bed till lunchtime.
她常常在床上呆到吃午餐時才起來。
You can take it as a given that there will be champagne at the wedding.
你可以假設婚禮上一定會有香檳。

NONE: › If someone would do something given half a chance, they would certainly do it if the opportunity came up.
只要有機會（就會做某事）

example: I'd give up work given half a chance.
只要有機會我就會辭掉工作。

NONE: › the name that is chosen for you at birth and is not your family name
（與姓相對的）名；（出生時取的）名字

example: Her family name is Smith and her given names are Mary Elizabeth.
她姓史密夫，名叫瑪麗‧伊利莎白。

NONE: › if I were allowed to, or if I could choose
要是允許我這樣做的話；要是讓我選擇的話

example: Given the chance, I'd spend all day reading.
要是讓我選，我會把一整天時間都用來讀書。
